title: Implement 90-degree clockwise matrix rotation in Rust
description: Implement rotate(matrix: &mut Vec<Vec<i32>>) that rotates an NxN matrix 90 degrees clockwise in place using transpose-then-reverse-rows.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement rotate in src/lib.rs using transpose-then-reverse-rows:
1. Transpose: for i in 0..n, for j in (i+1)..n, swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i]
2. Reverse each row: for each row in matrix.iter_mut(), call row.reverse()
All 4 test cases must pass.
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test --quiet` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test --quiet` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
